analysis: Examined three changes. (1) provider-swift/Package.swift head line 166-167 adds the `Hub` product from swift-transformers to ProviderCore. It comes from the already-trusted swift-transformers dependency (from: 1.3.0) and introduces no new package or URL. A broader floating dependency range is pre-existing. No provider-side trust boundary changes. (2) New provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift (head lines 1-312) is a CPU-only benchmark in the ProviderBenchmark target. It builds synthetic deterministic conversations (no real consumer data, A-001 not touched), loads a local tokenizer from a supplied model directory, and sets the prompt-token-cache verify env var to 0 only in a local copy of the environment. It uses random UUID prompt-cache scopes, so no cross-tenant scope is reused. It does not touch the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the keys, the coordinator WebSocket, or attestation. Output is local JSON of timings and token counts only. The benchmark is not on the serving path. It depends on ProviderCore symbols (PromptPreparationProbe, LocalTokenizerLoader, PromptTokenCachePolicy) that were not supplied here, so their security behavior could not be reviewed. (3) EngineV2Factory+BenchmarkPrompt.swift switches from separate decodeOpenAIRequest/extract* calls to a unified ProviderLoop.decodeInboundChatRequest(body) that returns the request plus extensions (template controls, sampling overrides, logprobs). The call sites are in the benchmark prompt path; the media rejection (MediaIngest.hasMedia) and the ToolChoicePromptPolicy remain in place. The security-relevant question for the next pass is the new decodeInboundChatRequest implementation in the production admission path, which was not in this batch. It should be checked for parity with the previous extraction (field validation, size limits, and the production path for template controls and sampling overrides). No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines.
